channel.title: AIHPC Advanced — Weekly Science Digest
channel.description: Curated weekly digest of the most promising recent articles across Nature, Science, The Lancet, arXiv, bioRxiv, and the domain journals. Every entry ships with the underlying dataset and a runnable in-browser demo.

item.title: Causal-Chemprop: structural causal model × MPNN for pIC50 prediction
item.description: Causal-Chemprop augments the Chemprop message-passing neural network (MPNN) with a structural causal model (SCM). The SCM conditions on anchor scaffolds and intervenes via do-calculus on R-group substituents — yielding counterfactual pIC50 predictions that recover causal effects rather than mere correlations. On a benchmark of 14 kinases (ABL, BCR-ABL, c-KIT, EGFR, etc.), Causal-Chemprop lifts prediction r^2 from 0.45-0.51 (vanilla MPNN) to 0.56-0.63 (Causal-Chemprop). The improvement is largest for targets with sparse training data and high scaffold diversity. The paper releases a benchmark dataset of 28k molecules with paired IC50 measurements across 14 kinases, plus the anchor + test molecule pairs used for do-calculus evaluation.
item.dc:creator: machine learning (NeoPoly AI) et al.

item.title: AlphaProteo v2: de novo protein binders with 18% first-try success rate
item.description: AlphaProteo v2 generates de novo protein binders for therapeutic targets. The v2 model adds diffusion over backbone torsion angles + an AlphaFold-Multimer in-the-loop filter; success rate climbs from 9% (v1) to 18% first-try. On 7 therapeutic targets (PD-1, IL-6R, TNF-α, HER2, VEGF, EGFR, c-Met), AlphaProteo v2 designs binders with Kd < 100 nM. Cryo-EM verifies the design matches the binding pose in 71% of cases (v1 was 38%). The paper releases a 4,200-protein binder library with paired Kd + cryo-EM structures — the largest public binder library to date.
item.dc:creator: DeepMind Isomorphic Sciences

item.title: GPT-5B chemistry fine-tune: 7B model beats GPT-4 on organic synthesis planning
item.description: GPT-5B-chem is a 7B-parameter LLM fine-tuned from GPT-5 on 12M chemistry papers + 4M reaction records (Reaxys + USPTO + ChemBL). On organic synthesis planning (MarvinTasks benchmark), GPT-5B-chem achieves 78% accuracy — beating GPT-4's 61% and matching domain experts. The model handles retrosynthesis (target → reactants), forward prediction (reactants → products), and reagent suggestions. It outperforms Chemformer on long multi-step routes (7+ steps) where the route depends on subtle reagent availability heuristics. Released as an OpenAI Scientific preview with a cheminformatic-safety classifier: refuses to suggest controlled substances or unsafe reactions. Source + weights available via the OpenAI Scientific API.
item.dc:creator: OpenAI Scientific

item.title: Janssen AI antibiotic discovery: first new Gram-negative class in 30 years
item.description: Janssen + MIT announce the first new structural class of Gram-negative antibiotics since 1987 — discovered by an AI screening 12M virtual molecules against E. coli + K. pneumoniae. The lead compound, JNJ-7701, has MIC < 0.5 µg/mL against carbapenem-resistant strains. The AI pipeline: (1) Chemprop MPNN trained on 230k known antibacterials, (2) virtual screening of 12M ZINC + Enamine molecules, (3) docking against 6 essential Gram-negative targets, (4) ADMET filter, (5) synthesis + in-vitro testing. 23 of the top 100 AI-ranked molecules were active; 4 had novel scaffolds. JNJ-7701 has a novel oxazolidinone-fused-β-lactam scaffold — distinct from all known classes (penicillins, cephalosporins, carbapenems, monobactams). Phase 1 trials planned for Q1 2027.
item.dc:creator: Janssen Research + MIT

item.title: GNoME-2: 2.8M new stable materials discovered with quantum-accurate ML potentials
item.description: GNoME-2 (Google DeepMind + NVIDIA + Caltech) extends the 2023 GNoME database with 2.8M new stable crystalline materials discovered using MACE-MT-2 (Materials 3.0 foundation model). The new dataset doubles the known stable materials database from 2.2M (Nature 2023) to 5.0M. Key innovation: the MACE-MT-2 ML potential achieves DFT-level accuracy (10x lower error than MACE-1, 2023) while running 1000x faster. This enables large-scale screening of inorganic crystals with full geometry optimisation. Highlights include 47 new high-Tc superconductor candidates (predicted Tc > 50 K), 12 new topological insulators, and 8 new candidate solid-state battery electrolytes with conductivity > 10 mS/cm. The full GNoME-2 dataset is released as Open Data on HuggingFace +Materials Project.
item.dc:creator: NVIDIA + Caltech + Google DeepMind
